title: St Joseph (19 March)
hook: the quiet carpenter, patron of workers and fathers

segments.voice: Yesterday, St Patrick, a kidnapped boy who went back, and your line was christ beside me.

Go through the Gospels looking for a single sentence spoken by Joseph, the husband of Mary. You'll come up empty. He has dreams. He gets up in the night. He takes a pregnant fiancée into his home, walks a family to Egypt and back, searches the city for a missing twelve-year-old. The text never once records him saying a word. Mary speaks. Simeon speaks. Angels speak. Joseph acts. After the stories of Jesus's childhood, he never appears in a scene again. Churches still give him a feast day. Today, St Joseph.
screen: `HE DREAMS. HE GETS UP. HE GOES.`

segments.voice: Matthew's story of Joseph opens at a painful moment. Mary, the woman he's promised to, is pregnant, and not by him. The King James Bible says: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Before any angel, his first instinct is to spare her shame, quietly. Then an angel comes in a dream and tells him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife. All Matthew gives of his response is this: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." No speech. No argument. He wakes up and does it. The pattern repeats. Another dream: take the child and flee. Matthew says he arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt. Up in the dark, packing, gone. Later, when the danger is over, home again. Then his work. In his home town, people later ask about Jesus, "Is not this the carpenter's son?" The Greek word behind carpenter means a builder or craftsman, someone who works with his hands. Mark calls Jesus himself the carpenter, so tradition pictures him learning the trade from this quiet man. That's why Catholics in particular honor Joseph as patron of workers, fathers and families. Some Orthodox and Protestant Christians honor him too, as the righteous man who sheltered the holy family. The picture is of faith that shows up mostly as getting up and doing the next thing.
screen: `A JUST MAN, MINDED TO SPARE HER SHAME.`
`RAISED FROM SLEEP, HE DID AS BIDDEN.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who looked after you and mostly showed up rather than talked: your father, if that's a good place to go, or a grandfather, an uncle, a coach, a neighbor who once fixed your bike and asked nothing for it. Let one thing they did come back clearly, and if you pray, thank God for them by name; if not, hold the memory with gratitude.
St Joseph. The husband of Mary and the carpenter of Nazareth, who in the Gospels never speaks, and keeps getting up to do what he was asked.
Your line: the quiet one. Not one word recorded. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the solemnity of St Joseph in March, and in parts of Italy and among Italian-American families, St Joseph's tables of food are set out and shared with the poor; Anglicans and some Lutherans also keep his day.

chat.says: Why does Joseph get a saint's day when he barely does anything in the Gospels?
options: He does plenty; he just never speaks. He protects Mary, gets up and acts.
He's honored for his sermons, which were saved outside the Gospels.
It's really a day for Mary; Joseph is added because he was her husband.
chat.meaning: The Gospels never record Joseph speaking, but he spares Mary shame, obeys his dreams and takes the family to Egypt. His faith shows in what he does.

Gospels.meaning: the four books that tell the life of Jesus

notes: 'The Gospels never record a word from Joseph': confirm (no direct speech of Joseph in Matthew or Luke).
'A missing twelve-year-old' comes from Luke 2:42 (cited text says 'twelve years old'); Luke 2:41–51 added to sources.
'Matthew says he arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt' is said in KJV words (Matthew 2:14) without quotation marks; cited as paraphrase. Confirm or quote.
τέκτων meaning 'builder, craftsman' is a lexicon meaning (e.g. BDAG/LSJ), not an etymology; confirm.
Patronage (workers, fathers, families) attributed to Catholics 'in particular'; Orthodox/Protestant honoring kept soft. Confirm.
Engagement/betrothal and 'the law is on your side' (fork) simplify first-century marriage law; confirm acceptable.

Editor: Joseph is named again later (e.g. 'Joseph's son' in Luke 4:22), so 'isn't mentioned again' became 'never appears in a scene again'; cut 'teaches a trade' from the list of things the Gospels show him doing; 'the worst moment of his life' softened; the workshop upbringing is now tradition, resting on Mark 6:3 (added to sources).

Editor 2: Luke says Mary and Simeon 'said', not sang (hook fixed); Matthew first names Joseph in the genealogy, so 'introduces him' reworded; Matthew 13:54 says 'his own country', not Nazareth, so 'the town of Nazareth' became 'his home town'; 'whatever the tradition, the picture is the same' softened.
